head: 1de824953d2e2cae0326bb505c334c75404218a5
scope: Issues 185, 193, and 194. A foreground lane router on port 18797 ran this code on Linux 7.0 x86_64, with its state on the machine's ext4 disk. It used the real accounts through copies of the dobby and work logins (lane.py, lane-config.json). The daily router kept running beside the lane, unchanged. A real claude -p request for claude-haiku-5-5 started a conversation. A lane restart over an events.jsonl that ended in a newline added no blank line. lane.py then stopped the lane and appended the first half of the last event line, as a short write leaves it. After the next restart, the first new event, model_catalog, began on a line of its own and parsed. A resume of the first conversation stayed on its account and kept its content, and digest.go's readDigest and account.go's requestsSince counted its request. The changes to the platform note and to activate's flags send no request. tests/test_claude_router_activate.py checks the platform note text and runs activate without the removed --agent-sdk flag. record.py built the record. Unchanged historical scenarios are references and were not rerun.

matrix.scenario: dobby token expires more than 4.5 h from now, outside the four-hour refresh lead
work token expires more than 4.5 h from now, outside the four-hour refresh lead
Lane code, executable, and SDK match the build at 1de8249 and go.mod
Both lane accounts are signed in with paid overflow disabled at start
The lane read the model catalog and serves claude-haiku-5-5
A new conversation for claude-haiku-5-5 is placed and answered through the lane
A restart over an events.jsonl that ends in a newline adds no blank line
Before the restart, events.jsonl ends mid-line with the first half of its last event
After the restart, the first new event starts on a line of its own and parses
After the restart, resuming the first conversation stays on its account and keeps its content
After the restart, the first new line decodes as the readers' claude.Event, and digest.go and account.go read past the partial line and count the resumed request

detail.method: lane_readers_test.go, added only to a temporary copy of the checkout, called readDigest (digest.go) and requestsSince (account.go) on the lane's events.jsonl after the restart, with the restart time as the window start. It also decoded the first new line with json.Unmarshal into claude.Event. Both readers decode each line the same way (digest.go:108, account.go:339). digest.go acts only on request and migrated events. account.go acts only on request events. Neither acts on the first new line, a model_catalog event, so a live run cannot show more than that decode.

matrix.scenario: claude-router cache reads the lane's events.jsonl after the restart
Identity is the same at the start and the end
The daily router kept running in the same process during the lane run

detail.method: lane.py hashed each refresh token in the daily login before it copied it, and again in the lane's copy after the last stop. It then deleted the copies. events.jsonl holds no credential_refresh event.

matrix.scenario: Evidence contains no copied access token

detail.method: Exact client token and the tokens in the lane's login copies, plus sk-ant-, JWT, and Bearer patterns, before the copies were deleted.
detail.rescan: A second scan covered every evidence file and accepted.json. rescan.json lists its files, method, and hits.

incidents.finding: lane.py expected the first event after a start to have kind "started", but the service writes the model_catalog event first, then the overage_read events, then the started event. The three rows that expected a started event failed. The router met their intent: after the restart over the partial line, the next byte was a newline and the first new line, model_catalog, parsed.
incidents.fixed_in: lane.py: those rows check that the first new line parses and record its kind

incidents.finding: An outside review of the second run's record found two problems. The readers row claimed that digest.go and account.go parse the first event after the restart. Their output cannot show that, because the first event is always model_catalog. Several other checks were also weaker than their row names.
incidents.fixed_in: lane.py. The readers row names what it checks and requires an exact count. The new conversation row requires the place decision and the answer. The resume row requires the first account on every request. The identity row requires the SDK version from go.mod. The paid overflow rows require both account IDs in status. A new row compares the daily router's process before and after the run.

incidents.finding: A review found that the third run's readers row no longer required the first new line to decode into claude.Event, as both readers decode each line. The third run's readers.json shows that the decode succeeded, but the row did not depend on it.
incidents.fixed_in: lane.py. The readers row requires that decode again. The fourth run's rows replaced the third run's.

prior_acceptance.status: historical reference, not rerun at this code
